name: Jump Search
description: Searches a sorted array by jumping ahead by fixed steps of √n, then performing linear search in the relevant block. Better than linear, simpler than binary.
aim: Jump √n steps at a time until a block containing the target is found, then search that block linearly.
howItWorks: Jump forward by step until arr[step] > target or end reached
Linear search in the previous block (from prev to step)

time.bestCase: Target found at first block check
time.worstCase: Target not present — check all blocks

complexity.spaceDescription: Uses only a few index variables

realWorld: Sorted databases where jumping is efficient
Systems where backward traversal is expensive
Alternative to binary search on magnetic tapes
whenToUse: When backward jump (binary search recursion) is expensive
Arrays on external storage where sequential reads are faster
alternatives: Binary Search — O(log n), better performance
Interpolation Search — O(log log n) for uniform distributions
Exponential Search — better when target is near beginning
